title: Development of an Integrated Speech Technology System for Afaan Oromo
institution: Hawassa University — Hawassa Institute of Technology
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
degree: Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering
abstract:
Cushitic languages such as Afaan Oromo spoken by over 50 million people in the Horn of Africa remain critically underrepresented in speech technology. While Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research for Afaan Oromo has progressed, the absence of Text-to-Speech (TTS) synthesis leaves existing systems fundamentally unidirectional.

This thesis addresses this gap through a comparative empirical evaluation of three neural TTS architectures — F5-TTS (flow-matching diffusion), VITS (variational inference with adversarial learning), and Fish Speech (codec-based language model) — across ten experimental configurations trained under Kaggle T4 GPU constraints.

The results demonstrate that architecture selection is more consequential than dataset scale for low-resource TTS: F5-TTS fails to adapt due to dominant English/Mandarin phonetic priors; unfrozen VITS training collapses into GAN-induced artifacts; whereas Fish Speech fine-tuned via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA r=32) combined with Retrieval-based Voice Conversion (RVC v2) achieves the highest naturalness and intelligibility, with a Mean Opinion Score (MOS) of 4.35 from a panel of ten native speakers.

Concurrently, the Whisper-Small ASR model was progressively fine-tuned on a corpus expanded to 101,518 pairs (~141 hours), achieving a Word Error Rate of 1.5% on the validation set.

The final system integrates ASR, TTS, and on-device Google ML Kit OCR into a unified FastAPI backend and cross-platform Flutter mobile application, deployed alongside four web applications on Hugging Face Spaces.
